Hi all,

Thanks for the context. High-level guidance:

- You can publish a private offer for any term length supported by the seller. If you want to move a buyer from 12 -> 36 months later, best practice is to publish a new private offer (amendments are not supported as a simple toggle). That said, sellers sometimes include an amendment path in the commercial paperwork — it's always treated as a new private offer for the marketplace management console.
- Typical AWS processing time for a properly completed private offer is 1-3 business days, but if legal needs to review marketplace-specific terms it can stretch to 5-10 business days.
- Co-sell paperwork (e.g., partner agreements) is separate and usually doesn't prevent the private offer but may delay finance activation for co-sell credits.

If you share the final pricing bands and the exact offer payload we can pre-check for missing fields to reduce processing time.

Regards,
Maya Singh
AWS Marketplace Enablement

Karthik — quick internal take:

- Pricing bands we typically present: 0% (list) for month-to-month / 12 months, ~12-18% off for 24 months, ~20-30% off for 36 months depending on committed ARR and payment terms. (See attached pricing_schedule_v2.xlsx)
- For legal: avoid marketplace-only contract language that changes payment recourse. Use our standard PO template and add an appendix that states the marketplace private offer id as the controlling sales instrument. That reduces buyer legal friction.
- If Acme insists on an amendment path, their legal will still treat it as a new offer; recommend we present both options: "12-month pilot" private offer with a predefined conversion discount for a 36-month commit (subject to new private offer execution). Explicitly call out conversion requires new PO signature to avoid surprises.

I'll draft the short playbook to share with Acme that lists timelines (1-3 days AWS processing, 7-14 business days buyer approvals typical), required docs, and the recommended language snippet.

1) Co-sell eligibility: We can confirm co-sell after the private offer is accepted and the buyer has an active contract. AWS co-sell credits require registered opportunities in the AWS portal before payout, so earlier registration helps.

2) Buyer finance activation: If Acme wants Redwood to invoice off-market (direct billing) rather than AWS invoicing, that will require an exception and additional finance review — plan for extra 7 business days. If they are fine with AWS-managed billing, the acceptance --> invoicing flow is quicker.
